_meta.about: Editable assumptions for Boond. Every value has a _why. Values marked ASSUMPTION are judgement calls; state them in the README.

rain._why_effective_threshold_ratio: Rain below 0.2 x ET0 is treated as lost to evaporation (the FAO-56 rule used in your spec, Ch. 8).
rain._why_skip_probability_threshold: ASSUMPTION: forecast rain counts toward SKIP only if Open-Meteo precipitation_probability_max >= 70 %. Null probability = not confident.
rain._why_forecast_rain_discount: ASSUMPTION: multiply forecast rain by this before using it for SKIP. Set 0.7-0.8 for a more cautious engine.

checkin._why_rain_mm: ASSUMPTION anchored to India Meteorological Department 24-h rainfall categories: light 2.5-15.5 mm, moderate 15.6-64.4 mm, heavy 64.5-115.5 mm. Values sit at or below each category's mid-point on purpose: under-counting rain makes Boond advise irrigation slightly early rather than late.
checkin._why_watered_mm: Fallback only; each crop in crops.json has its own irrigation.checkin_depth_mm. normal 75 mm = PAU Package of Practices 7.5 cm per irrigation; heavy 100 mm = PAU pre-sowing irrigation of ~10 cm; light 50 mm = ASSUMPTION (2/3 of normal; PAU says first wheat irrigation should be 'relatively light' without a number). Surface irrigation cannot be applied evenly much below ~40-50 mm per basin.

irrigation._why_light_depth_mm: Depth advised for HEAT PROTECTION. ASSUMPTION: smallest depth a farmer can spread over a levelled basin (kiara) with flood irrigation. The original 15 mm is only practical with sprinkler or drip.
irrigation._why_maximum_depth_mm: Cap on an IRRIGATE advice for upland crops = PAU's 7.5 cm per irrigation. Crop-level irrigation.max_advised_depth_mm overrides this (paddy uses 100 mm = PAU 10 cm standing-water limit).
irrigation._why_minimum_advised_depth_mm: ASSUMPTION: if the computed need is below this, round up to it (or WAIT) because smaller flood irrigations are not practical.
irrigation._why_application_efficiency: ASSUMPTION for gross pumping volume = net depth / efficiency. Use 0.6-0.75 for level-basin flood irrigation, ~0.9 for drip. Set to 1.0 if you want litres and kWh on the net depth only (as in the spec). Report which you used.

heat._why: Spec 6.5: warn if forecast Tmax reaches the threshold within 2-3 days while the crop is in a sensitive window.
heat._why_consecutive_days_required: ASSUMPTION. Raise to 2 for cotton and sugarcane, whose thresholds are crossed often in May-June.
heat._why_meaningful_rain_mm: ASSUMPTION: HEAT PROTECTION is not advised if at least this much confident rain is forecast inside the heat window, because the rain cools and wets the crop.

advisor._why_irrigate_within_days: Spec: IRRIGATE when depletion reaches RAW within the next 2 days, even after counting confident rain.
advisor._why_rain_skip_window_days: Spec: SKIP only when the field would reach RAW within 3 days without rain and confident rain keeps it below RAW for those 3 days. Later days of a 16-day forecast are reassessed on later days.
advisor._why_paddy_rain_skip_window_days: Paddy: only confident rain on the first forecast day can replace an irrigation that PAU's rule makes due (irrigate 2 days after the pond has gone).

kc_climate_adjustment._status: NOT IMPLEMENTED in the engine (future work: needs daily RHmin and mean 2 m wind). check_data fails if this is set to true, so nobody believes it is applied.
kc_climate_adjustment._why: FAO-56 Eq. 62 (Kc mid) and Eq. 65 (Kc end, only if the table value > 0.45): Kc = Kc_table + [0.04 (u2 - 2) - 0.004 (RHmin - 45)] (h / 3)^0.3, with u2 1-6 m/s, RHmin 20-80 %, h = max_crop_height_m in crops.json. Off by default so engine output matches the table values and your unit tests.
kc_climate_adjustment._why_wind_factor: FAO-56 Eq. 47: u2 = u10 x 4.87 / ln(67.8 x 10 - 5.42) = 0.748 x u10. Use a daily MEAN wind, not wind_speed_10m_max, if you enable this.

root_zone._why: Spec 6.4: Day 1 depletion = 0 because of the pre-sowing irrigation (PAU: ~10 cm rauni). Ask in onboarding; if the farmer says no pre-sowing irrigation, start at D = RAW (ASSUMPTION).

energy._why_default_pump_efficiency: ASSUMPTION (wire-to-water: motor x pump). Indian farm pumpsets are widely reported as inefficient; BEE's AgDSM programme estimates 30-40 % energy savings from star-rated replacements. Let farmers or a sensitivity range of 0.30-0.50 override it.
energy._why_m3: 1 acre = 4046.86 m2, so 1 mm over 1 acre = 4.047 m3 = 4,047 litres.
energy.kwh_formula: kWh = m3 x 9.81 x lift_m / (3600 x pump_eff)

carbon._why: CEA CO2 Baseline Database for the Indian Power Sector, Version 22.0 (Aug 2026), weighted average emission factor for FY 2025-26 = 0.675 tCO2/MWh (= kg CO2/kWh). Earlier years: FY24-25 0.710, FY23-24 0.727, FY22-23 0.716. This is a generation-side factor; it does not add transmission and distribution losses (ASSUMPTION: no T&D gross-up). Diesel pumps need a different factor.

cost._why: ASSUMPTION: a rough cost-of-supply proxy so savings can be shown in rupees, labelled as an estimate. What farmers actually pay is far lower: Punjab farm power is free to the farmer (state pays PSPCL; the agricultural subsidy is ~Rs 10,413 crore in FY 2025-26, Tribune), and Haryana's HERC 2026-27 order keeps tubewell tariff at 10 paise/unit. Present the rupee number as 'cost to the power system', not the farmer's bill.
